fields.customfield_25197:
Summary: WT-7912 Fix prefix search near optimisation to handle scenarios where the key range is split across pages.
Status: Closed
GA Released For OM/CM: Yes - 21/10/2022 (1467 Days Ago)
Assignee: Monica Ng

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents the functions of the product.
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
When we search for a key using the prefix search near optimization implemented in WT-7264 we early exit the search if {{__cursor_row_next_}} _or {{__cursor_row_prev}} return {{WT_NOTFOUND}}. However those functions return {{WT_NOTFOUND}} when they step to the end or the start of the page. As such if the prefix key_range extends across multiple pages the search will incorrectly return {{WT_NOTFOUND}} when in fact we should have found a value.

In order to fix this we'd need to differentiate between a prefix not found return and an end of page not found return. This could be implemented using a new WT error code.

I've written a python reproducer to demonstrate the flaw in the current algorithm:
{noformat}import time, wiredtiger, wttest, unittest
from wiredtiger import statdef timestamp_str(t):
    return '%x' % t# test_search_near01.py
# Test various prefix search near scenarios.
class test_search_near01(wttest.WiredTigerTestCase):
    conn_config = 'statistics=(all)'
    session_config = 'isolation=snapshot'    def get_stat(self, stat, local_session = None):
        if (local_session != None):
            stat_cursor = local_session.open_cursor('statistics:')
        else:
            stat_cursor = self.session.open_cursor('statistics:')
        val = stat_cursor[stat][2]
        stat_cursor.close()
        return val    def test_base_scenario(self):
        uri = 'table:test_base_scenario'
        self.session.create(uri, 'key_format=u,value_format=u')
        cursor = self.session.open_cursor(uri)
        session2 = self.conn.open_session()
        cursor3 = self.session.open_cursor(uri, None, "debug=(release_evict=true)")        # Basic character array.
        l = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"        # Start our older reader.
        session2.begin_transaction()        # Insert very large values so we fill the page content with less than 26 keys.
        # The key range that we search for will be a minimum of 26 keys.
        key_value = "abcde" * 100000
        key_count = 26*26*26
        # Insert keys aaa -> zzz.
        for i in range (0, 26):
            for j in range (0, 26):
                for k in range (0, 26):
                    cursor[l[i] + l[j] + l[k]] = key_value        # Evict the whole range.
        for i in range (0, 26):
            for j in range (0, 26):
                for k in range (0, 26):
                    cursor3.set_key(l[i] + l[j] + l[k])
                    cursor3.search()
                    cursor3.reset()        # Search near for the "aa" part of the range.
        cursor2 = session2.open_cursor(uri)
        cursor2.set_key('aa')
        cursor2.search_near()        skip_count = self.get_stat(stat.conn.cursor_next_skip_lt_100)
        # This should be equal to roughly key_count * 2 as the aa range will be traversed forwards
        # And then backwards, this assertion failing demonstrates the issue.
        self.assertGreater(skip_count, key_count * 2) {noformat}
In addition to fixing the code, the search near test created as part of WT-7924 should be executed with a more stressful configuration so keys are written across multiple pages. [This configuration|https://github.com/wiredtiger/wiredtiger/pull/7008/commits/6691f6c8e04c8c6dacc4189a2cd32029faac3e87] is a good start if not enough.

SERVER-61185 - Use prefix_search for unique index lookup
Status: Closed
Due Date: Not Set
Assignee: Louis Williams

Last Comment: Louis Williams - Over 49 months ago
This change improves the performance of inserting documents into collections with unique indexes. The change was not backported uniformly to all branches. For 4.4: We have disabled the optimized behavior by default, but it can be enabled with a setParameter "wiredTigerPrefixSearchForUniqueIndexes". This was done in an attempt to prevent making significant behavioral changes on a more stable branch. For 5.0: We have enabled the optimized behavior by default, but it can be disabled with a setParameter "wiredTigerPrefixSearchForUniqueIndexes". This may be done for users who do not want to expose themselves to this behavior on a stable branch. For all newer versions, this behavior is enabled by default and cannot be disabled.

comments.body: Do Basic testing , there is a follow on ticket for adding cppsuite stress test ( linked to this ticket)
Where is the ticket for the stress test?
[~kelsey.schubert], I've linked the follow on ticket.
Changed the relation between this ticket and the test ticket, so that test will be created first, before working on the solution.
[~vamsi.krishna], in that case, should we bring this ticket in sprint swapping this one?

Q1:
With prefix search enabled we should return the first visible match regardless of exactness.

Q2:
I think the suggestion is that we'd always place at the top of the prefix key range and therefore never need to traverse backwards?
I think that's true but would require special handling to avoid the prev loop in {{search_near}}, given that we traverse off the end in {{cursor_next}} we still traverse backwards again in {{cursor_prev}} so you'd expect the number of traversals to equal N*2 if N is the number of keys that have the prefix.

Also your suggested fix makes sense to me, assuming the key itself is still valid once you leave the cursor_row_next function.
Is this ticket related to WT-8280?

[~alexey.anisimov] the current thinking is that this ticket should resolve the failure mode seen on WT-8280, however due to uncertainty and wanting to reduce the amount of red in evergreen we've opted to disable the assertion in WT-8280 in the time being and will re-enable it after this ticket gets merged.
